## Context / Problem
`tests/unit/test_model_classes.py::test_a_finished_gate_drive_releases_its_event_loop[raised]` (added by 9ddb035cf59, bug waxy-nonspheral-cutworm) fails intermittently: `assert <_UnixSelectorEventLoop running=False closed=True> is None`. Seen in `make verify` on branch veery-verify-identity-perf (host load ~16; 1 failed, 21,400 passed) and in CI `Verified` for Gerrit 3431 (run 44417947610, job 135204371707, pytest ubuntu py3.12: 1 failed, 21,343 passed). Both parametrized cases pass in isolation. It blocks `Verified +1` for unrelated changes.

Root cause (reproduced): anyio's `WorkerThread` (anyio/_backends/_asyncio.py) holds `self.loop = root_task._loop`. When the root task finishes, `WorkerThread.stop` only enqueues a `None` sentinel; the worker thread exits on its own schedule. `_drive_on_fresh_thread` joins only its own drive thread, then the test calls `gc.collect()`. If the anyio worker has not exited yet, its thread object still references the closed loop. Scratch reproduction: wrapping `WorkerThread.run` to linger 0.5 s after the sentinel makes the loop survive `gc.collect()`; joining the worker threads (and dropping the reference) first makes it collectable.

## Approach
In `_drive_on_fresh_thread`, record `threading.enumerate()` before starting the drive thread; after it joins, join every thread that is new since then (the anyio workers it started), with a 10 s join bound so a wedged worker fails the test instead of hanging, and keep no reference to them. Then return the weakref. This keeps the test's real claim (with anyio>=4.15 nothing but a still-running worker holds the loop) and removes the timing race. Add a regression test that monkeypatches `WorkerThread.run` to linger 0.3 s after its sentinel and asserts the loop is still collected. Test-only; no config key, env var or flag.

Rejected: `time.sleep` before `gc.collect()` (still a race); retrying.

Portability: threading and gc only; the existing `importorskip("anyio.to_thread")` stays.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_model_classes.py` — `_drive_on_fresh_thread` joins the drive's new threads; one new regression test.

## Testing
- New regression test with a lingering `WorkerThread` fails before the fix (RED) and passes after.
- Existing `completed` and `raised` cases pass.
- `make verify` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `_drive_on_fresh_thread` joins the anyio worker threads started by the drive before returning.
- [x] A regression test that delays `WorkerThread` exit fails on the old helper and passes on the new one.
- [x] `make verify` passes and the change lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
